newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe to announce new duties by end of January.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe to announce new duties by end of January.

text.p: Zimbabwe's government will introduce tariffs by the end of January to protect industries from a flood of cheaper imports, Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa said on Tuesday.

He told a news conference the announcement of the tariffs, introduced last July but withdrawn after a week, had been delayed by thorough government checks to ensure there were no errors before printing the tariff book.
Local industrialists, who have clamoured for years for duties to protect them from cheaper imports, were expecting an announcement this week.

"The tariff regime has been approved by cabinet. What remains are the tariff books which are being printed. We wanted to ensure that there were no errors. This is the delay in printing the tariff books," Murerwa said. "We are hoping that by the end of the month these should be ready."
He declined to comment in detail on revisions to the tariffs which the government said were needed when it withdrew them last July, saying these were aimed at curbing dumping.
